subproblem.title: Moment factor: (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ (∫_{M_0}(h+ε)^{n/(n−1)} dμ)^{1/n}
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 2 and ℓ ∈ ℕ, and let μ be a measure on E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Borel σ-algebra) that is finite on compact sets. Let h: E → ℝ be continuous, nonnegative and compactly supported, and let ε > 0 and t ≥ 0. Put p := n/(n − 1) and M_s := {x : h(x) > s}, and write μ(M_t) for the real measure μ.real(M_t). Then (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} · μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ (∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ)^{1/n}. All powers are real powers (Real.rpow) of nonnegative bases, and ∫_{M_0} is the Bochner set integral.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (ε t : ℝ), 2 ≤ n → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → Continuous h → HasCompactSupport h → (∀ x, 0 ≤ h x) → 0 < ε → 0 ≤ t → (t + ε) ^ ((n : ℝ) - 1)⁻¹ * (μ.real {x | t < h x}) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ ≤ (∫ x in {x | 0 < h x}, (h x + ε) ^ ((n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) ∂μ) ^ (n : ℝ)⁻¹
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra. For A ⊆ E, μ[A] ∈ [0, ∞] is the measure of A and μ(A) = μ.real A is its real value (the toReal of μ[A]). ∫ denotes Bochner integrals (0 for non-integrable integrands) and ∫⁻ lower Lebesgue integrals of [0, ∞]-valued functions. ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is y ↦ max(y, 0), dt is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, and x^y is the real power Real.rpow (used only with bases x ≥ 0). Source: step 4 of the parent proof (the 'trivial inequality' on the last page of the proof of Simon 5.7, p. 100), with the parts of parent steps 1 and 3 that it uses. Notation: p := n/(n − 1), K₀ := tsupport h, Q := ∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ.

1. (Exponents.) As a real number n ≥ 2, so n > 0 and n − 1 > 0. Hence p = n/(n − 1) ≥ 0, 1/n ≥ 0, and p·(1/n) = (n/(n − 1))·(1/n) = 1/(n − 1). Also t + ε ≥ 0 because t ≥ 0 and ε > 0.
2. (Sets.) Since h is continuous, M_t and M_0 are open, hence Borel. If x ∈ M_t then h(x) > t ≥ 0, so x ∈ M_0; thus M_t ⊆ M_0. If x ∈ M_0 then h(x) ≠ 0, so x ∈ support h ⊆ K₀; thus M_t ⊆ M_0 ⊆ K₀. K₀ is compact because h has compact support, so μ[K₀] < ∞ (μ is finite on compact sets), and therefore μ[M_t] ≤ μ[K₀] < ∞.
3. (Integrability.) The function x ↦ (h(x) + ε)^p is continuous on E: h + ε is continuous and, because p ≥ 0, y ↦ y^p is continuous. It is ≥ 0 everywhere, since h + ε ≥ ε > 0 (Real.rpow_nonneg). A continuous function is integrable on a compact set for a measure that is finite on compact sets (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact). So (h + ε)^p is μ-integrable on K₀, and therefore on its subsets M_0 and M_t. The constant (t + ε)^p is integrable on M_t because μ[M_t] < ∞.
4. (Moment inequality.) Integrating a constant over a set of finite measure gives (t + ε)^p μ(M_t) = ∫_{M_t} (t + ε)^p dμ. For x ∈ M_t we have h(x) + ε > t + ε ≥ 0. Since y ↦ y^p is nondecreasing on [0, ∞) for p ≥ 0 (Real.rpow_le_rpow), (t + ε)^p ≤ (h(x) + ε)^p. Both functions are integrable on the measurable set M_t, so monotonicity of the set integral (setIntegral_mono_on) gives ∫_{M_t} (t + ε)^p dμ ≤ ∫_{M_t} (h + ε)^p dμ. Next, M_t ⊆ M_0 and (h + ε)^p is nonnegative and integrable on M_0, so monotonicity in the domain (setIntegral_mono_set) gives ∫_{M_t} (h + ε)^p dμ ≤ ∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ = Q. Altogether (t + ε)^p μ(M_t) ≤ Q.
5. (n-th roots.) The left side of step 4 is ≥ 0, because (t + ε)^p ≥ 0 and μ(M_t) ≥ 0. Since y ↦ y^{1/n} is nondecreasing on [0, ∞) (1/n ≥ 0), ((t + ε)^p μ(M_t))^{1/n} ≤ Q^{1/n}. For x, y ≥ 0 we have (xy)^{1/n} = x^{1/n} y^{1/n} (Real.mul_rpow). Since t + ε ≥ 0, ((t + ε)^p)^{1/n} = (t + ε)^{p·(1/n)} = (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} by step 1 (Real.rpow_mul). Hence (t + ε)^{1/(n−1)} μ(M_t)^{1/n} ≤ Q^{1/n} = (∫_{M_0} (h + ε)^p dμ)^{1/n}. ∎
proof_key_steps: M_t ⊆ M_0 ⊆ tsupport h (compact), so μ[M_t] < ∞ and the continuous (h+ε)^p is integrable on M_0
Raise both nonnegative sides to the power 1/n; (xy)^{1/n} = x^{1/n}y^{1/n} and ((t+ε)^p)^{1/n} = (t+ε)^{1/(n−1)}
